assessment.nobel_worthiness: Pd-catalysed C-N cross-coupling turned aryl amine construction from a harsh, substrate-limited problem into a routine, general transformation. Ligand design (bulky biaryl phosphines, hindered alkylphosphines) made it broadly applicable, and the reaction is used daily in medicinal chemistry, process chemistry and materials synthesis. This is the kind of general bond-forming method I weigh most heavily; what was new chemically is clear.
assessment.attribution: Buchwald and Hartwig developed the general catalytic systems and the mechanistic understanding in parallel from 1994-95 on. Kosugi's earlier tin-amide coupling is a genuine precursor and creates a priority question, but the practical, general method is the Buchwald and Hartwig work. A two-person prize is cleanly supportable.
assessment.maturity: Three decades of independent confirmation, thousands of applications and large-scale industrial use. Recognition is arguably overdue, and it fits well with the 2010 cross-coupling prize as a distinct, later conceptual advance.
uncertainties: Whether the committee views this as too close to the 2010 Pd cross-coupling prize.
Weight to give Kosugi's earlier precursor work; I am working from memory, not verified.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Selective C-H functionalization lets chemists treat C-H bonds as functional groups, shortening syntheses and enabling late-stage modification. Directing-group, ligand-accelerated and template-controlled approaches solved the selectivity problem, which was the real obstacle. This goes straight to efficiency in synthesis.
assessment.attribution: The field is broad. Yu is the clearest owner of ligand and template control of selectivity. Sanford and Hartwig made decisive contributions to Pd and Ir/B catalytic C-H functionalization, and Daugulis, Smith and others also have claims. A three-person prize is feasible but will exclude real contributors, and the credit split is the main difficulty.
assessment.maturity: Widely used in academia and increasingly in pharma, but industrial adoption is still maturing, so recognition is somewhat early. The best single transformations are well confirmed.
uncertainties: Which of several overlapping contributions (Pd, Ir, Rh, template chemistry) is decisive.
Hartwig's overlap with B055 could count against a double recognition.
Extent of routine industrial use is uncertain.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Visible-light photoredox catalysis opened radical and single-electron pathways under mild conditions, and it is now standard in discovery chemistry and in dual catalysis with nickel and other metals. It is a real reordering of what is considered routine synthetically.
assessment.attribution: Credit is spread over MacMillan, Yoon and Stephenson (2008-2011 independent starting points), with Nicewicz, Melchiorre, Konig and Fukuzumi contributing. MacMillan already holds a prize for organocatalysis, which complicates a prize to him. Yoon and Stephenson alone would be a defensible but unconventional pairing.
assessment.maturity: Rapid adoption and large independent confirmation. Still evolving, and some of the reagent chemistry has older roots in inorganic photochemistry, so timing is plausible but not obviously final.
uncertainties: Whether MacMillan's 2021 prize reduces appetite for this candidate.
Priority relative to older photoredox work (Kellogg, Fukuzumi, Cano-Yelo and Deronzier) is disputed.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Native chemical ligation joins unprotected peptides chemoselectively, making total chemical synthesis and semisynthesis of proteins possible. It is a conceptually simple, chemically novel reaction that created access to proteins that were not made before, with modified, labelled and unnatural structures.
assessment.attribution: Dawson, Muir and Kent (with Kent's group at Scripps) published the 1994 Science paper, with Kent as the main conceptual driver. Muir's expressed protein ligation is a distinct extension that fits the semisynthesis scope. Danishefsky, Brik and Liu are important for later developments, but I regard the three as the core credit.
assessment.maturity: Three decades old, with extensive independent use in chemical biology and in synthesis of therapeutic proteins. Mature and timely.
uncertainties: Whether the committee treats this as a chemical-biology advance rather than core chemistry.
Wide use is clear for research, but industrial-scale manufacturing impact is less so.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Phosphoramidite chemistry gave reliable, fast, high-yielding automated oligonucleotide synthesis. It underpins PCR primers, sequencing, gene synthesis and oligonucleotide drugs, and it is a stereo- and chemoselective method that remains the industrial standard after four decades.
assessment.attribution: Caruthers developed the phosphoramidite method (Beaucage and Caruthers, 1981, and subsequent work). Hood's credit is for automation and instrumentation, which I would treat as a separate contribution. A single-laureate prize is supportable but the history involves other groups (Letsinger, Khorana).
assessment.maturity: Very mature and extremely widely used. If anything it is long overdue, and there is a risk that the best moment to recognise it has passed.
uncertainties: Beaucage's co-credit is not in the supplied names.
Contribution of Letsinger, and the automation by Hood and others, is not resolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Targeted protein degradation by heterobifunctional PROTACs and molecular glues is a new chemical modality that uses the ubiquitin system to remove proteins, and it opens up targets considered undruggable. It is chemically interesting, though chemical novelty is mostly in medicinal-chemistry design.
assessment.attribution: Crews and Deshaies conceived and demonstrated PROTACs. Ciulli contributed the VHL ligands and structural rationale. Handa, Ito and others have a strong claim for the thalidomide and cereblon glue mechanism, which is a real conflict that makes the allocation hard.
assessment.maturity: Clinical trials are underway but approvals are still absent, so the long-term impact is not yet proven. Recognition might be premature for a chemistry prize.
uncertainties: No approved PROTAC drug yet, to my knowledge.
Split between heterobifunctional and molecular-glue credit.
Fit between chemistry and medicine remains uncertain.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: ATRP made controlled radical polymerisation robust and general, giving access to defined architectures, block copolymers and functional materials from ordinary monomers with simple catalysts. It is a widely used synthetic method in polymer chemistry, and the chemical idea (reversible halogen atom transfer under metal catalysis) is simple.
assessment.attribution: Matyjaszewski (with Wang) and Sawamoto (with Kamigaito) reported the method independently in 1995. Equal contributions justify a pairing of Matyjaszewski and Sawamoto, though Kamigaito and Wang are also credited. RAFT, a separate candidate on the list, would compete for the same polymer-chemistry slot.
assessment.maturity: Thirty years of use and independent confirmation. Industrial uptake exists but is less universal than for cross-coupling.
uncertainties: Competition with RAFT and nitroxide-mediated routes for one polymer-chemistry prize.
Wang's role relative to Kamigaito is unresolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Frustrated Lewis pairs showed that sterically hindered main-group acids and bases can activate H2 and other small molecules without metals, and catalyse hydrogenation. It is a conceptually new reactivity principle, with clear chemical novelty.
assessment.attribution: Stephan reported the 2006 metal-free H2 activation, and Erker contributed key related chemistry (intramolecular FLPs, small-molecule capture). A two-person prize is clean and well supported by the supplied credit.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed in many labs and now used in catalysis, but the synthetic usefulness has not reached the breadth of the leading methods above. Probably still maturing.
uncertainties: Practical impact on synthesis is smaller than the conceptual impact.
Contributions of earlier related work (Brown, Wittig, Tochtermann) are not resolved.
